label: Great aurora of 17 Nov 1848
intensity_note: min QD geomag lat 29.5 deg (St Croix; Lockwood rank 19); H variation >400 nT at Prague (Valach)
source: Lockwood, Owens, Brown & Vazquez 2025 MNRAS 540:3596; Valach et al. 2019 JSWSC 9:A11; 'Timelines...' JSWSC 11:29 (2021) Table 1 ('Europe and America'); Silverman NE-US/SE-Canada daily logs 1848-1853 cover this date

label: Carrington precursor storm
intensity_note: equatorward boundary 36.5 deg ILAT (Hayakawa 2018); min QD lat 16.7 deg (Panama; Lockwood rank 2); inferred max -Dst ~673 nT (Love et al. 2025)
source: Hayakawa et al. 2018 ApJ 869:57; Lockwood et al. 2025; Love, Mann, Qvick & Mursula 2025 Space Weather e2024SW004286; Green & Boardsen 2006 Adv Space Res 38:130 (US/N. America sightings)

label: Carrington storm (great storm)
intensity_note: boundary 32.7 deg ILAT multicolour / 30.8 deg ILAT red (Hayakawa 2018); min QD lat 18.4 deg (Lockwood rank 4/5); Dst est ~ -900 to -1000 nT (Cliver & Svalgaard 2004; Love 2025: 964 nT)
source: Cliver & Svalgaard 2004 Solar Phys 224:407; Hayakawa et al. 2018 ApJ 869:57; Hayakawa et al. 2019 Space Weather 17 (doi 10.1029/2019SW002269); Green & Boardsen 2006; Green et al. 2006 Adv Space Res 38:145

label: Great aurora of Oct 1870
intensity_note: min QD lat 22.0 deg (Giza/Cairo; Lockwood rank 8); max aaH 368 nT; 2 SSCs; telegraph disruption in Iberia
source: Ribeiro, Vaquero, Gallego & Trigo 2016 Space Weather; Lockwood et al. 2025

label: Great storm of Feb 1872 (Chapman-Silverman storm)
intensity_note: most extensive aurora in 1650-2024 record: min QD lat 5.9 deg (Khartoum; Lockwood rank 1); 24.2 deg ILAT boundary from Shanghai (Hayakawa 2018); Dst est < -830 nT; aaH 626 nT
source: Hayakawa et al. 2018 ApJ 862:15; Hayakawa et al. 2023 ApJ (doi 10.3847/1538-4357/acc6cc); Lockwood et al. 2025; Silverman 2008 JASTP (US reports likely; not re-verified here)

label: Electric storm of Nov 1882
intensity_note: -Dst est ~386 nT; 4-day mean aa 214 nT (highest since 1868); visibility ~39 deg MLAT (JSWSC 2021 Table 2); US telegraph disruption
source: Love 2018 Space Weather 16 (doi 10.1002/2017SW001795)

label: Superstorm of Oct/Nov 1903
intensity_note: Dst' min ~ -531 nT; equatorward boundary ~44.1 deg ILAT
source: Hayakawa et al. 2020 ApJL 897:L10

label: Superstorm of Sep 1909
intensity_note: Dst min -595 nT; boundary 31-35 deg ILAT (400 km) to 37-38 deg; min QD lat 27.2 deg (Matsuyama; Lockwood rank 14)
source: Hayakawa et al. 2019 MNRAS 484:4083; Love, Hayakawa & Cliver 2019 Space Weather 17:37 (2019SpWea..17...37L)

label: New York Railroad superstorm
intensity_note: max -Dst 907+/-132 nT on 15 May; overhead aurora to ~40 deg geomag, horizon to ~30 deg (Silverman & Cliver 2001); min QD lat 30.2 deg (Jamaica; Lockwood rank 20); aaH 831 nT
source: Love, Hayakawa & Cliver 2019 Space Weather 17:1281; Silverman & Cliver 2001 JASTP 63:523 (uses US Climatological Data aurora notes)

label: Storm sequence of Jan 1938 (Fatima storm 25-26 Jan)
intensity_note: Dcx -171 (17/18), -328 (21/22), -336 nT (25/26); boundary 40.3/40.0 deg ILAT; min QD lat 26.5 deg (Tunisia; Lockwood rank 13); aaH 656 nT
source: Hayakawa et al. 2021 ApJ 909:197

label: Severe storm of Apr 1938
intensity_note: Dcx -255 nT; visibility ~41 deg MLAT
source: 'Timelines as a tool for learning about space weather storms' JSWSC 11:29 (2021) Table 2 (cites Nicholson & Sternberg-Mulders 1939)

label: Easter storm of Mar 1940
intensity_note: Dst est ~ -389 nT (20 UT 24 Mar); boundary <=46.3 deg ILAT; US power/communication impacts
source: Hayakawa et al. 2021 MNRAS (doi 10.1093/mnras/stab3615)

label: Storm of Feb/Mar 1941
intensity_note: Dst* ~ -464 nT (conservative); boundary 38.5 deg ILAT (East Asia)
source: Hayakawa et al. 2021 ApJ 908:209

label: Geomagnetic blitz of Sep 1941
intensity_note: Dcx -404 nT (Lockwood) / -359 nT (JSWSC 2021); K=9 at Cheltenham MD; min QD lat 27.8 deg (Tunis; Lockwood rank 15)
source: Love & Coisson 2016 Eos (aurora reported as far south as New Mexico); Lockwood et al. 2025

label: Storm of Mar 1946
intensity_note: Dst* <= -512 nT; boundary <=41.8 deg ILAT
source: Hayakawa et al. 2020 MNRAS 497:5507

label: Storm of Sep 1946
intensity_note: Dcx -163 nT (strong, not great)
source: 'Timelines...' JSWSC 11:29 (2021) Table 2 (cites Araki 2014)

label: Storm of Aug 1950
intensity_note: Dcx -260 nT; min QD lat 30.8 deg (photographic, Greece; Lockwood rank 21)
source: Lockwood et al. 2025

label: Storm of Jan 1957
intensity_note: Dcx -255 nT; min QD lat 23.7 deg (Canary Is.; Lockwood rank 9); aaH 416 nT
source: Lockwood et al. 2025

label: Great storm of Feb 1958
intensity_note: Dst -426 nT (Kyoto); red aurora seen to Mexico City (19.4N); min QD lat 26.3 deg (Japan; Lockwood rank 12)
source: Kataoka & Kazama 2019 JSWSC 9:A28; 'Timelines...' JSWSC 11:29 (2021) Table 1; Lockwood et al. 2025

label: Storm of Nov 1960
intensity_note: Dst -339 nT (Kyoto, 13 Nov; largest of 1960) - index value only, no peer-reviewed aurora study found
